<description>
AvailableCoins() takes an optional CCoinControl pointer that defaults to nullptr, and the other uses of it check for null first. The TRUC version filter added in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/ec2676becdf488f7a1151345a019c05dec926308 does not, so a call without coin control dereferences a null pointer as soon as the wallet has an unconfirmed output in the mempool.

Found this issue with few seconds of fuzzing with the change in the second commit which adds wallet transactions in the mempool state with a fuzzed version, and call `AvailableCoins()` directly with an optional null coin control.
</description>

<commits>
6a5577f100 wallet: guard null coin control in AvailableCoins TRUC filter

AvailableCoins() takes an optional CCoinControl pointer that defaults to
nullptr, and the other uses of it check for null first. The TRUC version
filter added in ec2676becd does not, so a call without coin control
dereferences a null pointer as soon as the wallet has an unconfirmed
output in the mempool.

No current caller hits this: RPCs, the GUI and CreateTransaction always
pass a coin control, and the tests and benchmarks that use the default
only have confirmed coins.

Treat a missing coin control like one that does not request a TRUC
transaction, and add a test that calls AvailableCoins() with the default
argument on a wallet with an unconfirmed transaction.

032be32485 fuzz: cover unconfirmed outputs and null coin control in spend target

Add wallet transactions in the mempool state with a fuzzed version, and
call AvailableCoins() directly with an optional null coin control, an
optional fuzzed feerate and fuzzed filter params, including
min_sum_amount and max_count to reach the early-return paths.
</commits>
